findings.text: the served plan view still runs unpassed_gate_blockers over every gate, so a plan whose only open gate is a closure gate renders as blocked while reckon/roadmap.py:1070 reports the same plan in ready_now, and that divergence is reachable only because this change introduced transition gates.
the MCP blocking projection makes the same unfiltered call, so mcp_blocking carries a closure gate as a blocker beside the roadmap's own closure_blockers entry for that one gate.

a pending decision-lockable gate forces its decision row to open, and reckon/roadmap.py:1084 makes any open decision remove the plan from ready_now, so of the two transitions this change models as one edge the decision one idles the plan while the plan-terminal one does not.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against c924a244; e280d50f adds the tests, figure and docs, 3fb14fb2 lands the schema, plan-HTML read/write, store refusals and roadmap derivation, e1d2c312 repairs sparse legacy serialisation, and 8ff3d41f plus c563da20 are documentation, with every path inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the measure asks for both directions plus an executed negative control, and tests/test_closure_gates.py carries the ready direction at :70-80, the refusal at :84-100 and the accepted-after-verdict direction at :104-121, with the control at negative-control.log.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a plan carrying a closure gate that stays dispatchable while a terminal write is refused until the gate has a verdict; reckon/roadmap.py:1083 filters transition gates out of the execution blockers so the plan reaches ready_now, and reckon/_store.py:2028-2040 refuses the write naming the gate and its gating plan.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names the five commits, nine changed paths, both suite arms with their failure ids and the declared-mutation log, and its counts reproduce against baseline.log (8 failed, 2747 passed) and current-head.log (7 failed, 2784 passed).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the dispatch fenced eight paths and this diff touches nine; the ninth, docs/_shared/plan.schema.json, is covered by the recorded user scope extension in scope-extension.json, and the worktree is clean at c563da20.

justifications.durability: the declared mutation recorded at negative-control.log:1 and :3 removes the refusal call in reckon/_store.py and reddens tests/test_closure_gates.py:84-100 across all seven terminal statuses, but the control covers one of the three refusal points (reckon/_store.py:1998, :2109 rest on their own assertions).
justifications.evidence: the gate ran and its result is on disk, but the head arm recorded in after_suite is revision 8ff3d41f rather than the reviewed head c563da20, so the reviewed head is covered by the docs-only argument in the manifest checkpoint rather than by a log taken there.
justifications.fit: reckon/_store.py:2104 reuses the terminal-set detection shape that reckon/_store.py:2067 already uses, the guarded model_serializer at reckon/_schema.py:731 keeps legacy gate records sparse, and no plan or sprint label reaches the source; the deduction is the unfiltered blocker list at reckon/serve.py:1866.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/roadmap.py:1083 keeps a transition-gated plan in ready_now and dispatchable while reckon/_store.py:2028 refuses that plan's terminal write naming gate and gating plan, so the goal is met on the roadmap; the deduction is that reckon/serve.py:1866 answers the same question the other way.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in `git diff --stat c924a244..c563da20` lies inside the dispatch fence or the extension recorded in scope-extension.json, and no commit carries anything the goal does not imply.
